newsitem.title: CHINA: SHANGHAI SOYBEANS END DOWN ON SPECULATIVE SELLING.
newsitem.headline: SHANGHAI SOYBEANS END DOWN ON SPECULATIVE SELLING.

text.p: Shanghai soybean futures ended down across the board on Tuesday on speculative selling by retail investors, traders said.
The most actively traded September 1997 contract ended at an intraday low of 3,164 yuan ($382), losing 11 yuan. It opened at a high of 3,170 yuan per tonne.
November fell three yuan to 3,148, the January 1998 contract five to 3,110 and March six to 3,106 per tonne.
Combined volume fell to 16,300 tonnes from 19,100 tonnes.
Soybeans opened mostly down and moved in a narrow range for most of the session, traders said.
"Speculative selling by retail investors dominated trading today and further falls are likely," one trader said.
"Market sentiment is very weak as most investors have little interest in trading on such a dull market," he said.
Traders said they expected soybeans to fall steadily in the next few days.
